outcomes.text: Analyse phonetics, phonology and prosodics: how speech sounds and effects are articulated.
Analyse lexis and semantics: English vocabulary, including social and historical variation.
Analyse grammar and morphology at sentence, clause, phrase and word level.
Analyse pragmatics: the contextual aspects of language use.
Analyse discourse: extended stretches of communication in different genres, modes and contexts.

topics.title: Section A: Language under the microscope

subtopics.title: Close analysis of a short written text

outcomes.text: Identify significant features and patterns in an unseen text and explore their effects.
Explore the effect of lexical choices and grammatical features.
Explore how contextual factors shape the production and reception of a text.
Apply language concepts and methods of analysis systematically to data.
Use language terminology accurately and refer accurately to texts and sources.

topics.title: Section B: Writing about a topical language issue

outcomes.text: Show critical understanding of issues and concepts relevant to language use.
Evaluate attitudes towards language and its users.
Show how texts and discourses are shaped by genre, mode and context.
Write short original pieces for a real-world purpose, form and audience.

topics.title: Section C: Comparing and contrasting texts

outcomes.text: Compare spoken and written texts, spontaneous and crafted speech, and different forms of spoken English.
Compare individual and social varieties of English and British regional dialects.
Apply theory, such as gender or power, to linguistic features when comparing texts.
Explore connections across texts and how the areas of study link across the course.
Analyse a short sample of authentic children's speech from ages 0 to 7.
Read phonemic transcription using the International Phonetic Alphabet.
Apply theories of child language acquisition to interpret the data.
Apply knowledge of the language levels to data with accurate terminology.

topics.title: Section B: Language in the media

outcomes.text: Explore how power is represented in a variety of texts and discourses.
Explore how gender is represented and reproduced in texts and discourses.
Explain how modes of communication shape language varieties and affect use beyond that mode.
Apply language concepts and theories to the linguistic and graphological features of a multi-modal media text.
Evaluate language use in different genres, modes and contexts, drawing the areas of study together.
Describe how English has developed and changed over time, including methods for studying language change.
Study a range of historical texts and genres.
Identify and compare significant features in texts from two different times.
Compare how contextual factors affect production and reception in each text.
Critically evaluate attitudes towards language and its users.
